subject: mathematics
question_text: If f: R − {0} → R is defined by f(x) = x³ − 1/x³, show that f(x) + f(1/x) = 0.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.9, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 4. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape gives one mark to writing f(1/x) correctly and one to the addition that cancels, because the whole question turns on 1/(1/x)³ = x³. recall_prompt: Say how you would show this — what you substitute, and what happens when you add.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write f(1/x)
steps.margin_note: First mark is f(1/x) written out. The step that earns it is 1/(1/x)³ = x³. Say that 1/x is in the domain, since x ≠ 0 makes 1/x ≠ 0 as well.
steps.memory_tip: 1/x cubed is 1/x³, and 1 divided by 1/x³ is x³. The two terms simply swap places.

recall.must_convey: That replacing x by 1/x gives f(1/x) = 1/x³ − x³, using 1/(1/x)³ = x³.
accept: replace x by one over x so f of one over x is one over x cubed minus x cubed
one divided by one over x cubed is x cubed so the two terms swap
substitute the reciprocal into the same rule
x badulu one by x pedithe terms swap authai
f of the reciprocal is one over x cubed minus x cubed

steps.why: The whole proof is one substitution. Putting 1/x where x stands turns x³ into 1/x³ and turns 1/x³ into x³, so f(1/x) is f(x) with its two terms exchanged. The domain R − {0} matters here: it is what makes 1/x a legal input.
common_mistakes: Using x = 0, which the domain R − {0} does not allow.

steps.label: Add the two expressions
steps.margin_note: Second mark is the addition shown ending at 0. Write the added line first; jumping straight to 0 gives the examiner nothing to mark. Check with x = 2: f(2) = 63/8 and f(1/2) = −63/8.
steps.memory_tip: f(1/x) is f(x) with a minus sign in front, so the sum must be 0.

recall.must_convey: That adding the two expressions cancels x³ with −x³ and −1/x³ with 1/x³, leaving 0.
accept: add them and x cubed cancels with minus x cubed and the other pair cancels too
the two expressions are negatives of each other so the sum is zero
x cubed minus one over x cubed plus one over x cubed minus x cubed is zero
rendu terms cancel ayi zero vasthundi
everything cancels in pairs and the total is zero

steps.why: Adding the two expressions pairs x³ with −x³ and −1/x³ with +1/x³, so every term cancels. That is what the statement means: f(1/x) is the negative of f(x), for every x in R − {0}.
common_mistakes: Substituting one number such as x = 2 and stopping; a single value is a check, not a proof.
Cancelling one pair of terms and leaving the other pair on the page.
Writing the answer as 0 with no added line above it.
